channel.title: Halt updates
channel.description: New versions of Halt for Windows. Written by tools\Publish-Release.ps1.

item.title: Halt 0.11.0
item.description: • Buy Halt Pro right from the app: "Get Halt Pro" opens the checkout in your browser, and once you have paid, Halt switches to Pro by itself within a few seconds. There is no key to copy.

item.title: Halt 0.10.0
item.description:
• Blocks the websites you choose in Chrome, Edge, Brave and Firefox, including private windows, using the browsers' own policy settings.
  • Closes blocked apps and games within 2 seconds of opening, with a short message saying why.
  • Locks: a timer lock in Halt Basic, and in Halt Pro a wait, a long random text, a restart, or a password someone else keeps.
  • Schedules that start blocks on their own, plus breaks and daily allowances.
  • Adult content filter for the whole PC with SafeSearch locked, a cool-down you set in advance, and a Permanent mode.
  • One switch to block YouTube Shorts, Instagram Reels and Facebook Reels.
  • Stats, a weekly challenge and one-tap site bundles.
  • Halt Pro licenses, activated on up to 3 PCs.
  • Automatic updates: Halt checks for a new version once a day and installs it when no session is running, without changing your settings.
  • Lock this PC (Halt Pro): keeps the whole computer on the Windows lock screen for a time you choose, up to 12 hours, even after a restart. There is no early stop, and Safe Mode always lets you back in.
  • Light mode: choose Dark, Light, or System (follows Windows) in Settings > Theme.
  • Halt waits in the tray by the clock when its window is closed or minimized, with the session's countdown in the tooltip; click the icon to open it again. Off in Settings > Start-up and tray if you prefer.
  • Start with Windows (off by default): Halt opens in the tray when you sign in, with no window and no admin prompt.
  • A slimmer hourglass frame: rounded metal rods and capped discs, lit, and the glass sways instead of spinning.
  • The hourglass's sand is your session's time: one grain for every second, and one grain falls each second, so the sand at the bottom is exactly the time that has passed.
  • Daily time limits (Halt Pro): cap how long you use a site, app or bundle each day, for example YouTube for 2 hours or Spotify for 6. When you reach the cap it's blocked for the rest of the day, and only the lock you chose (timer, delay, text, restart or password) can lift it early. A site counts while it's the tab in front of you, an app while it's in front or playing sound (so music counts), and time away from the PC doesn't. Limits reset at midnight and run all day without a focus session. There's a new Limits tab.
  • Block a single page, channel or playlist, not just a whole site: add an entry like youtube.com/@name or youtube.com/watch?list=... to your blocked or allowed list.
  • Block Task Manager and the Command Prompt during a focus session (Halt Pro), so a session can't simply be killed. It's switched off in Settings by default, clears the moment the session ends, and never gets in the way of uninstalling Halt.
  • A free 7-day Halt Pro trial: the first install on a PC unlocks everything for 7 days, with no card and no account. After that Halt keeps working as Halt Basic, and the Pro settings you made wait for a license. The header shows the days left, and the trial runs once per PC, even after reinstalling.
  • Halt opens without the Windows admin prompt. The Halt service now runs the part that changes protected settings, and the app window runs with your normal rights. "Start with Windows" works the same way.
